text:
Ibrahim A: hey everyone, day 2 here. i merged the company kubeconfig and tried to `kubectl config use-context redwood-dev` but when i `kubectl get pods -n rl-telemetry` i get a forbidden pointing at `system:serviceaccount:default:ibrahim-sa`. not sure why my user is being replaced by that SA. any pointers?
Ben (DevEx): welcome Ibrahim! quick check: run `kubectl config view --minify -o jsonpath='{.contexts[?(@.name=="redwood-dev")].context.user}'` and `kubectl config view users -o jsonpath='{.users[*].name}'`. might be a context that sets a user to that SA.
Ibrahim A: outputs: `system:serviceaccount:default:ibrahim-sa` for the first, and users list has `ibrahim@example.com system:serviceaccount:default:ibrahim-sa`. i guess the merge duplicated entries.
Ben (DevEx): yep. when merging kubeconfigs some teams use a shared SA entry for CI which can get copied. easiest fix: edit `~/.kube/config` and remove the unwanted user block, or set the context to your Okta user: `kubectl config set-context redwood-dev --user=ibrahim@example.com`. also ensure KUBECONFIG env merge didn't override `current-context`.
Ibrahim A: tried `kubectl config set-context redwood-dev --user=ibrahim@example.com` and then `kubectl auth can-i list pods -n rl-telemetry` returns `no` (user not in team).
Ben (DevEx): that means auth is working but RBAC denies you — expected for new hires. two options: (1) finish identity sync so you're added to team-telemetry, or (2) request a personal namespace to iterate quickly. Sam, can infra provision a sandbox for ibrahim?
Sam K: will do. also FYI, if you need to verify which token is used by the client, run `kubectl config view --raw --minify` and check the `user.token` or the exec output. sometimes mac keychain stores an old token too.
Ibrahim A: identity sync status? identity-bot: Identity sync for ibrahim@example.com: pending consent.
Ibrahim A: i clicked the consent link in the onboarding UI now. how long to propagate?
Sam K: usually 5-10 minutes. i'll create `ibrahim-dev` and bind a scoped role so you can deploy the sample consumer. infra-bot: Created INFRA-5012 to provision namespace ibrahim-dev and bind edit to system:serviceaccount:default:ibrahim-sa (ETA ~8m).
Ibrahim A: thanks — that'd unblock me. curious: what's the recommended pattern for local testing vs team namespaces?
Ben (DevEx): recommended flow: (1) request personal namespace `dev-<yourname>` for dev work, bind `edit` to your SA; (2) use team namespaces only for integration tests after you're added to the team group; (3) avoid editing production RoleBindings yourself; open an INFRA ticket for scoped role requests. docs: https://redwood.dev/onboarding/k8s-access has the checklist.
Ibrahim A: infra-bot updated: INFRA-5012 completed, namespace `ibrahim-dev` created. tried `kubectl auth can-i create deployments -n ibrahim-dev` -> yes. creating a test deployment now.
Sam K: quick tip — when merging kubeconfigs, prefer `KUBECONFIG=~/.kube/config:~/.kube/onboard kubectl config view --merge --flatten > /tmp/merged && mv /tmp/merged ~/.kube/config` to avoid accidental user duplication.
Ibrahim A: works great. deployed the sample consumer to `ibrahim-dev` and port-forwarded to test locally. thanks for the quick help! :thumbsup:
